title: Sealed Proof Claim Assembler: packaged key-provenance + residency + retention evidence
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a deterministic, verifiable bundle called the 'Sealed Proof Claim' that assembles cryptographic key provenance (KMS/HSM signing metadata), tenant data residency assertions, and retention-policy snapshots into a single signed artifact suitable for customer audits and regulator submission. The bundle must be compact, tamper-evident, and easy for internal and customer-side verification. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and an initial opt-in UI in Console for downloading the artifact per tenant and time-range.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and Compliance
Backend implementation can produce a Sealed Proof Claim for a given tenant and time window within SLA (<= 30s for small snapshots)

Claims include: key IDs, wrap/unwrapping events, KMS/HSM signer cert chain fingerprints, region tags for affected storage, retention policy versions and timestamps, and an integrity signature produced by Redwood's evidence-signing key

Artifact format is JSON-LD with a deterministic canonicalization step and a detached Merkle root summary; verification tooling (CLI) can validate signature and contents using only public evidence-signing key
Unit and integration tests covering rotation overlap windows, multi-region residency, and partial-data retention cases
A Console button to request/download Sealed Proof Claim is available behind feature flag and logs usage to auditing stream
Security review completed and artifacts stored encrypted at rest with access logged
implementation_steps: Finalize format: choose JSON-LD + canonization + signature scheme (ECDSA-P384 or ED25519) after Security consult
Design backend pipeline: gather KMS/HSM event stream + retention-policy config + storage location map for tenant and time range
Build compressor/normalizer to collapse similar events and produce deterministic ordering
Compute Merkle tree over event entries and produce root; include root in signed envelope
Integrate with Evidence Signer service (new API to request one-off signatures for claim envelopes)
Expose API endpoint: POST /v1/tenants/:id/sealed-proof-claims with range + reason -> returns signed bundle or job id
Console flow: request modal, show estimated size/time, download link when ready
Implement CLI verifier that accepts bundle and public key to validate integrity and extract human-readable summary
Add end-to-end tests including simulated KMS rotations and cross-region file moves
Roll out feature behind gate; stage to private deployments before Hosted
decisions: Use JSON-LD to allow schema evolution and easier mapping to customer audit schemas (Security approved on 2026-02-18)
Prefer ED25519 for evidence signing for smaller signature size; fallback to ECDSA-P384 for customers that require it
Include a detached Merkle root instead of storing full Merkle proofs in the artifact to keep payload small; provide optional full proof export when requested
Retention snapshots will include policy id/version + effective_since + effective_until rather than raw policy deltas to make auditing deterministic
open_questions: Should the bundle include tenant-provided key fingerprints for BYOK scenarios, or only Redwood-managed key metadata? (Security leaning towards including both optionally)
What retention period should we keep generated bundles server-side for customer re-downloads before purging? (proposal: 90 days)
Do regulators require notarization from third party in target markets (EU/UK)? If yes, what integration scope?
Edge case: how to represent events that span rotation boundaries where data encrypted under multiple KEKs exists? (design suggests enumerating artefact-level encryption epochs)
Operational: who rotates the evidence-signing key and how will that be tracked in claim history?
